This behaviour looks to have started recently, so I wonder if anything could have changed on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> that may have prompted it.

To be clear here, the purpose of shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is to host Shiny applications. When that application is actually RMarkdown, shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> will treat it as an RMarkdown Shiny document and use rmarkdown::run to launch it. If you use that command locally, you should encounter exactly the same situation as when you deploy to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

If you are simply looking for a way to host the static output of rendering a non-interactive RMarkdown site, you might be better off pursuing GitHub Pages or Netlify.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joshua - Thanks for the further query.

N is declared in the main script and assigned a list of brands, and then viewed to ensure that the data is there. Script updated to encode the text as UTF8 for compatibility in Shiny

N <- enc2utf8(SWrnames)
View(N)

Then in the Shiny App, N is used as the source for the drop-down menu, with the chosen brand stored as 'SKU'

      selectInput(inputId = "SKU",
                label = "Select a Scotch Whiskey:",
                choices =  N,
                multiple = FALSE,
                selectize = FALSE,
                width = '400px',
                size = NA),
      textOutput("result")

Then in the output section, the chosen brand, SKU, is matched against N, the list of brands, to give the index number of the chosen brand to then select the appropriate brand's data to pull into the chart:

   output$scatterPlot <- renderPlot({
    View(input$SKU)
    Choice <- match(input$SKU,N)
    View(Choice)

    Xvar <- ObservedOverExpected[Choice]
    Yvar <- Observed[Choice]

    XYPlot <- data.frame(Xvar,Yvar)

    X<- XYPlot[1]
    Y<- XYPlot[2]

    ggplot(XYPlot, aes(Xvar, Yvar))  + geom_point() +geom_smooth() + ggtitle(N[Choice]) +xlab("Observed over Expected") +ylab("Observed") + geom_text(label=SWrnames, color="#008b30", size=2, nudge_x = 0.00, nudge_y = 0.00, check_overlap = T)

Works like a charm on my PC, but N not recognised as a variable on the Shiny server. Any help on this appreciated!

Best regards,

David

First of all, thank you for bearing with us in this delay. Historically new versions of R were made available for Ubuntu on CRAN just a few days after the regular release, and we were caught flat-footed; our apologies.

In order to support R 3.5.0 and to have more control in the future, on 5/31/2018 we will be updating the base system that we provide on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> from Ubuntu 14.04 (trusty) to Ubuntu 16.04 (xenial). Initially only new applications and new deployments of existing applications will take advantage of this. If you run into any issues while deploying your application after this change, please reach out to us (here, or at shinyapp...@rstudio.com if you are on paid plan) and we will be happy to assist.

As an additional benefit of this change, the issues with the tensorflow and keras packages that surfaced when pip 10 was released also appear to have been resolved.

Thank you again for your patience,

The shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> team
